text:
Forty minutes at Little Caesars Arena produced no goals and very little to choose between the teams. The third produced three, and the last one belonged to Trevor Connelly, who snapped home the winner with 1:42 left to give Vegas a 2-1 win it probably owes Carter Hart a thank-you card for.

Vegas had the first period, out-chancing Detroit 1.22 to 0.38 in expected goals, the quality of each side's chances, but Daniil Tarasov kept it scoreless. Detroit pushed back in the second, 1.26 to 0.74, and Hart held his ground. When the scoring finally came, it came from unlikely places. Anton Johansson, a defenseman playing 9:36, opened it 2:02 into the third on an 8% chance, with Carter Mazur and Sheldon Dries assisting. The Red Wings went from a 52% chance of winning to 77%.

Braeden Bowman answered 2:18 later. He reached the NHL undrafted, by way of Henderson in the AHL, and his 6% snap shot off a Tomas Hertl and Victor Olofsson setup tied it. Then the game turned on a save. With 8:23 left and the score 1-1, Hart stopped Viktor Arvidsson on a 52% look, the best chance of the night that didn't go in.

Connelly made it count. Jack Eichel and Rasmus Andersson set up his 14% snap shot at 18:18, and Vegas went from 48% to 89%. Connelly, the 19th pick in 2024, had 49 points in 46 AHL games for Henderson last season, and in 11:18 here he scored the goal that decided the night.

But the honest version of this game is that Detroit did enough to win it. Replay every shot and the Red Wings win 55% of the time. Hart faced 26 shots worth 3.03 expected goals and allowed one, saving 2.0 goals more than expected; by our wins-added measure he was the most valuable player on the ice. Tarasov was good too, saving 0.76 more than expected on 34 shots. Detroit's power play went 0 for 2 despite 0.95 expected goals, and a team that loses a game it carried late will feel this one for a day or two.
headline: Connelly and Carter Hart steal one in Detroit
